chunks: And from him, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abu al-Maghra', from Sama'a, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

If I were appointed guardian over the people, I would surely teach them how it is proper for them to divorce. Then I would not have a man who had violated (the ruling) brought to me except that I would inflict pain upon his back.
And whoever divorces contrary to the Sunnah shall be referred back to the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, even if his nose is forced into the dust.

key_terms.السُّنَّةِ: The Sunnah — the established prophetic practice governing divorce procedure
key_terms.رَغِمَ أَنْفُهُ: His nose was humiliated — Arabic idiom meaning 'even against his will'
key_terms.كِتَابُ اللَّهِ: The Book of God — the Quran, which contains the foundational rules for divorce
key_terms.وَلِيتُ: To be appointed wali/guardian — political and jurisprudential authority over a community
key_terms.يَنْبَغِي: It is befitting/proper — indicating legal propriety

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about divorce contrary to the Sunnah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) asserts his authority and mastery over Islamic divorce law, declaring that if he held political authority over the people, he would enforce correct divorce procedure and punish those who violated it. The phrase 'regretting his nose' (رَغِمَ أَنْفُهُ) is a classical Arabic idiom meaning 'even against his will' or 'even if he is humiliated.' This hadith comes in the context of the Imams' teachings that divorce not performed according to the Sunnah is invalid and must be corrected according to Quranic guidelines.
